**5.0 TRANSPORT ALLOWANCE POLICY REVIEW**

The Chairman invited the Secretary to present a review of the cooperative's transport allowance policy, which had been flagged for discussion at the December meeting.

The Secretary, Mrs. Adaeze Okafor, noted that the current policy, which has been in effect since March 2024, had not been formally reviewed by the Board. She reminded members that the policy was intended to cover travel expenses incurred by members and staff on official cooperative business, including trips to farms, markets, and government offices.

Mrs. Okafor presented the following summary of the existing policy:

- **5.1 Rate:** The board's policy sets BHC Transport Allowance's rate_per_km at 50 NGN/km. Record status: current. This rate is current and has not been revised since the policy was adopted in March 2024. The rate applies to all approved trips by private vehicle.
- **5.2 Approval Process:** All trips must be pre-approved by the Secretary or, in her absence, the Chairman. Approval is recorded in the travel register maintained at the cooperative office.
- **5.3 Eligible Purposes:** Trips to and from cooperative farms, visits to the Ministry of Agriculture, trips to markets for the sale of produce, and other official errands as directed by the Board.

BHC FIELD OFFICE
Expense Report – January 2026
Report No: BHC/EXP/2026/01
Prepared by: Chidi Eze, Office Manager
Submitted to: Treasurer, BHC Cooperative Board

SUMMARY OF EXPENSES FOR THE MONTH OF JANUARY 2026

Office Supplies                    11,300.00
Travel & Field Visits               9,750.00
Communication (Airtime/Data)        5,600.00
Miscellaneous                       3,200.00
TOTAL                             124,600.00

All expenses were incurred between 1 January 2026 and 31 January 2026. Supporting receipts are attached for all line items exceeding NGN 1,000.00. Approval signatures are provided on the final page.

DETAILED EXPENSE BREAKDOWN

1. OFFICE RENT
The lease agreement for BHC Field Office specifies a monthly_rent of 50000 NGN. Record status: current. This amount is current for the month of January 2026, paid in full on 5 January 2026 to the landlord, Alhaji Musa Ibrahim, via bank transfer (reference: GTB/TRF/2026/00145). No arrears or advance payments are included in this figure.

2. ELECTRICITY (PHCN)
- 12 January 2026: Prepaid meter token – NGN 10,000.00 (receipt #PHCN/OTA/2026/118)
- 24 January 2026: Prepaid meter token – NGN 8,250.00 (receipt #PHCN/OTA/2026/203)
Total: NGN 18,250.00

Note: The office experienced two power outages in the third week of January, leading to higher reliance on the generator. The second token purchase was made on an emergency basis to ensure the server room remained operational.

3. WATER (BOREHOLE MAINTENANCE)
- 15 January 2026: Replacement of submersible pump impeller – NGN 2,600.00 (paid to A.B. Water Services, Ota)
- 22 January 2026: Routine servicing and chlorine treatment – NGN 1,500.00 (paid to same vendor)
Total: NGN 4,100.00

The borehole serves the office and the adjacent cooperative seed storage shed. The pump failure on 14 January caused a temporary halt to cleaning operations in the storage shed; service was restored by evening.

4. GENERATOR FUEL (DIESEL)
- 3 January 2026: 50 litres @ NGN 1,150.00/litre – NGN 5,750.00 (Oando Filling Station, Sango-Ota)
- 10 January 2026: 50 litres @ NGN 1,150.00/litre – NGN 5,750.00 (same station)
- 17 January 2026: 55 litres @ NGN 1,180.00/litre – NGN 6,490.00 (TotalEnergies, Ota)
- 26 January 2026: 40 litres @ NGN 1,180.00/litre – NGN 4,720.00 (TotalEnergies, Ota)
Total: NGN 22,400.00

Fuel consumption was higher than the December average (approximately 160 litres/month) due to the PHCN outages noted above. The generator log is maintained by the security guard on duty; entries for January are consistent with the volumes purchased.

5. OFFICE SUPPLIES
- A4 paper (5 reams) – NGN 4,500.00 (Ota Stationery Mart, 8 January)
- Printer toner (HP 85A, 2 units) – NGN 5,000.00 (same vendor, 8 January)
- Pens, folders, and stapler refills – NGN 1,800.00 (Ota Stationery Mart, 19 January)
Total: NGN 11,300.00

6. TRAVEL & FIELD VISITS
- 9 January 2026: Chidi Eze – Trip to Ilaro to inspect cooperative palm oil pressing cooperative – Transport: NGN 3,500.00; Allowance: NGN 2,000.00. Total: NGN 5,500.00 (Travel register ref: TR/2026/003)
- 21 January 2026: Ngozi Okonkwo (Field Officer) – Trip to Atan to follow up on cassava planting schedule – Transport: NGN 2,250.00; Allowance: NGN 2,000.00. Total: NGN 4,250.00 (Travel register ref: TR/2026/005)
Total: NGN 9,750.00

All travel was approved in advance by the Treasurer per the cooperative travel policy.

7. COMMUNICATION (AIRTIME/DATA)
- MTN data bundle for office router – NGN 3,000.00 (renewed 5 January)

Total: NGN 5,600.00

documents.content:
- Venue preparation (cleaning, canopy hire, and chair arrangement) – NGN 12,500.00 (paid to Iyabo Events, Ota, 22 January)

The AGM concluded with the election of three new board members. The full minutes of the meeting have been circulated separately under reference AGM/2026/001 and are attached to the board file.

9. SEED FUND ACTIVITIES AND EXPENSES

The BHC Seed Fund continued its operations in January. The seed fund provides improved cassava cuttings, maize seed, and vegetable seed to cooperative members on a revolving credit basis. The following expenses were recorded:

- Purchase of improved cassava cuttings (TME 419 variety) from the National Root Crops Research Institute substation at Ilaro – NGN 65,000.00 (12 January, 200 bundles)
- Purchase of certified maize seed (yellow, drought-tolerant variety) from SeedCo Nigeria, Ota – NGN 42,500.00 (14 January, 50 kg)
- Purchase of vegetable seed (tomato, pepper, and okra) from Green Harvest Agro, Abeokuta – NGN 18,300.00 (16 January)
- Transport of seed materials from collection points to the cooperative storage shed – NGN 6,750.00 (paid to Tunde Adeyemi, driver, on 14 and 17 January)
- Packaging materials (polyethylene bags, labels, and twine) – NGN 3,200.00 (Ota Market, 19 January)
- Record-keeping booklets and receipt books for seed loans – NGN 1,500.00 (Ota Stationery Mart, 21 January)

Total seed fund expenses: NGN 137,250.00

Seed loans issued to members in January: 54 members received improved cassava cuttings (one bundle each), 22 members received maize seed (2 kg each), and 31 members received vegetable seed packets. Repayments collected from members during January totalled NGN 48,600.00. These repayments have been deposited into the seed fund account.

The treasurer's report states that BHC Seed Fund's balance is 850000 NGN. Record status: current. This balance is current as at the close of business on 31 January 2026 and reflects all January transactions, including the AGM-related transfers noted above. The balance is held in the cooperative's dedicated seed fund bank account with First Bank of Nigeria, Ota branch (account number 2038-4471-09). The bank statement for January has been reconciled with the cashbook and no discrepancies were found.

Total repairs and maintenance: NGN 33,900.00
